subtitle: From Doorkeepers to Guardians of the North

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a rugged frontier fort under stormy skies
panels.action: Nagabhata I stands on the ramparts of a stone fort in the arid hills of western India, wind whipping his cloak as distant armies gather below and a vast northern plain stretches beyond the gates he watches.

dialogue.text: They called themselves Pratiharas, doorkeepers—yet in a century they claimed to guard all the north. How did a frontier house of uncertain origin come to stand between India and the world?

i18n.hi: खुद को प्रतिहार, यानी द्वारपाल कहते थे, पर सौ साल में बोले – पूरा उत्तर हमारी पहरेदारी में है। सीमा पर बैठे इस अनजानी कुल ने हिंद व दुनिया के बीच जगह कैसे बना ली?

panels.shot: slow push-in over an engraved stone inscription lit by flickering lamplight
panels.action: A worn stone slab lies in a temple-like hall, its Sanskrit letters deeply carved, while a brazier’s flame throws moving shadows over the script of the Gwalior Prashasti.

dialogue.text: Our trail begins not in Nagabhata’s lifetime, but a century later, in the Gwalior Prashasti of Mihira Bhoja—where memory, ambition and stone shape the story of who the Pratiharas were.

i18n.hi: हमारी कहानी नगभट्ट के ज़माने से नहीं, सौ साल बाद से चलती है – मिहिर भोज की ग्वालियर प्रशस्ति से, जहाँ याद, महत्वाकांक्षा और पत्थर मिलकर प्रतिहारों की कहानी गढ़ते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of court poets in a royal hall presenting a copperplate to seated nobles
panels.action: In a 9th-century court, bearded Brahmana poets hold up a freshly inscribed stone or copperplate before attentive courtiers, as a scribe kneels and copies the text.

dialogue.text: The inscription praises a line of kings who, it says, sprang from Lakshmana, Rama’s brother, the one who stood guard as doorkeeper. From this, it explains, came the name Pratihara.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख एक वंश की तारीफ करता है जो, कहता है, लक्ष्मण से निकला – राम का भाई, द्वार पर पहरा देने वाला। इसी से, वह समझाता है, नाम पड़ा प्रतिहार।

panels.shot: close-up on the carved word 'Pratihara' beside a small relief of Lakshmana standing guard
panels.action: The camera focuses on the chiselled letters of “Pratihara” and a carved figure of Lakshmana at a doorway, his hand on a bow, in low relief on the inscription slab.

dialogue.text: This is courtly genealogy, not verifiable blood. It ties a new power to an old epic, wrapping recent rulers in the prestige of the Ramayana, and turning a common title into a sacred duty.

i18n.hi: ये दरबारी वंशावली है, साबित खून का रिकॉर्ड नहीं। नया राज बल से नहीं, रामायण की शान से जुड़ता है, ताज़ा शासकों को पुराने महाकाव्य के आँचल में लपेट कर, एक साधारण पदवी को पवित्र फर्ज बना देता है।

panels.shot: wide map-like aerial of western India with Jalor-Bhinmal, Avanti and the northwestern frontier highlighted
panels.action: A stylized landscape shows the arid hills around Jalor and Bhinmal, the plateau of Avanti, and the open northwest frontier, paths of caravans and armies drawn faintly across the terrain.

dialogue.text: Yet the true beginnings of the Pratiharas rise from earth, not legend—from the Jalor–Bhinmal region and the western frontier, where deserts met trade routes and invasions tested every wall.

i18n.hi: लेकिन प्रतिहारों की सच्ची शुरुआत ज़मीन से उठती है, कथा से नहीं – जालोर–भीनमाल और पश्चिमी सरहद से, जहाँ रेगिस्तान, व्यापार मार्ग और हमले हर किले की परख लेते थे।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a Jain monk dictating to a scribe in a small monastery at Jalor
panels.action: Inside a modest Jain monastery, Uddyotana Suri sits cross-legged, calmly dictating as a young scribe writes on a palm-leaf, the fort of Jalor glimpsed through a small window.

dialogue.text: Around 778, in Jalor’s shadow, the Jain writer Uddyotana Suri composed the Kuvalayamala. His story-world, filled with names and places, quietly fixes this frontier as the Pratiharas’ early stage.

i18n.hi: लगभग ७७८ में, जालोर की छाया में जैन लेखक उद्द्योतन सूरी ने ‘कुवलयमाला’ लिखी। उनके पात्र, नाम और जगहें चुपचाप दिखा देती हैं – यही सरहद प्रतिहारों का शुरुआती रंगमंच थी।

panels.shot: split composition showing an older map placing the centre at Ujjain contrasted with the Jalor-Bhinmal focus
panels.action: On one side, scholars in a study trace a circle around Ujjain on a parchment map; on the other, a later scholar points instead to Jalor and Bhinmal, rearranging markers.

dialogue.text: Older historians saw Ujjain and Avanti as the cradle of Pratihara power. New readings of texts and inscriptions pull our gaze westward, to Rajasthan’s rugged passes and trading towns.

i18n.hi: पुराने इतिहासकार उज्जैन और अवंती को प्रतिहार ताकत की जननी मानते थे। पर नए पाठन और लेख हमें पश्चिम की ओर खींचते हैं – राजस्थान के खुरदरे दर्रे और कारोबारी कस्बों की तरफ।

panels.shot: medium shot of young Nagabhata I training with weapons in a frontier fort courtyard
panels.action: A younger Nagabhata I, broad-shouldered and intent, practices spear and sword drills in the dusty courtyard of a frontier fort, elders watching from the shade of a stone wall.

dialogue.text: Into this contested belt steps Nagabhata, first of the line we can see clearly. The records do not name his childhood, but they show a man whose world was walls, watchtowers and approaching dust.

i18n.hi: यहीं खिंचे हुए क्षेत्र में कदम रखता है नगभट्ट – वह पहला प्रतिहार जिसे हम साफ देख पाते हैं। रिकॉर्ड उसके बचपन का नहीं, पर एक ऐसे आदमी का दिखाते हैं जिसकी दुनिया बस किले, मीनारें और उठती धूल थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Nagabhata I overlooking caravans and distant horsemen from a hilltop
panels.action: Nagabhata I stands on a rocky hill, looking down at a caravan winding through the valley as a band of mounted warriors appears on the horizon.

dialogue.text: This was no quiet interior kingdom. It was a frontier—between plateau and desert, between old clans and newcomers, between the settled towns of Rajasthan and the open routes that led to the northwest.

i18n.hi: ये कोई शांत अंदरूनी राज्य नहीं था। ये सरहद थी – पठार और रेगिस्तान के बीच, पुराने कुलों और नवागतों के बीच, बसे हुए राजस्थानी कस्बों और उत्तर–पश्चिम को जाती खुली राहों के बीच।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of a mixed army mustering near a desert outpost
panels.action: An army gathers near a desert outpost: infantry with spears, archers, and cavalry under standards, as Nagabhata I rides along the line, appraising the men with a steady gaze.

dialogue.text: Some later texts speak of Nagabhata’s clashes with powerful foes, even with the tide of Arab expansion pressing from Sind. Whatever the exact battles, the pattern is clear—this house rose as a shield on the edge.

i18n.hi: कुछ बाद के ग्रंथ नगभट्ट की टक्कर को ताकतवर दुश्मनों से जोड़ते हैं, यहाँ तक कि सिंध से फैलती अरब लहर से। भले सटीक लड़ाइयाँ धुंधली हों, पैटर्न साफ है – ये घराना किनारे पर एक ढाल बनकर उठा।

panels.shot: close-up on Nagabhata I in council with elders and Brahmana advisers in a stone hall
panels.action: In a dim stone hall, Nagabhata I sits on a low throne while grey-haired chiefs and Brahmana advisers gesture over a rough map laid on the floor.

dialogue.text: But swords alone could not hold this space. Nagabhata’s time belongs to an early medieval India where power hardened into lineages, titles, and grants—where rulers needed not just forts, but stories.

i18n.hi: लेकिन सिर्फ तलवारें ये जगह नहीं थाम सकती थीं। नगभट्ट का ज़माना वही आरंभिक मध्‍यकालीन भारत था, जहां ताकत वंश, उपाधियों और दानों में जमने लगी – और शासकों को केवल किले नहीं, कहानियाँ भी चाहिए थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a royal grant being issued to Brahmanas with a village landscape in the background
panels.action: A royal officer hands a copperplate grant to a group of Brahmanas, while behind them a village with fields and a small temple stretches under the sun.

dialogue.text: Across the subcontinent, chiefs conferred land and revenue on religious specialists, gaining ritual backing and written charters. Names like Pratihara, Paramara and Chauhan began to fix into enduring houses.

i18n.hi: पूरे उपमहाद्वीप में सरदार भूमि और राजस्व धर्म–विशेषज्ञों को देते, बदले में यज्ञ, विधि और लिखित सनद पाते। प्रतिहार, परमार, चौहान जैसे नाम धीरे–धीरे टिकाऊ कुलों में ढलने लगे।

panels.shot: close-up of an inscription mentioning Nagabhata and 'Gurjaras' being read by a scholar
panels.action: A modern scholar runs a finger along a stone inscription, pausing over the names Nagabhata and 'Gurjaras' etched into the surface.

dialogue.text: One inscription, from Gallaka in 795, says Nagabhata conquered the Gurjaras. Yet later writers speak of his line as Gurjara-Pratihara. The very word ‘Gurjara’ shifts, blurring between people, place and power.

i18n.hi: ७९५ की गल्लक की एक शिलालेख कहती है – नगभट्ट ने गुर्जरों को हराया। पर बाद के लेखक उसकी ही वंश को गुर्जर–प्रतिहार कहते हैं। ‘गुर्जर’ शब्द खुद ही फिसलता है – कभी लोग, कभी जगह, कभी सत्ता।

panels.shot: wide conceptual shot showing different groups and labels across a stylized map, slightly overlapping
panels.action: A stylized map shows small figures representing clans and communities, with the label ‘Gurjara’ hovering over one region and then sliding toward the Pratihara name, the overlap left deliberately hazy.

dialogue.text: We cannot pin the dynasty to a single, certain ethnicity. Gurjara might mean a region, a confederation, or a political identity. The Pratiharas’ rise helped give that name weight, but did not freeze its meaning.

i18n.hi: इस वंश को किसी एक पक्की जाति से बाँध नहीं सकते। गुर्जर शायद इलाका हो, संघ हो या राजनीतिक पहचान। प्रतिहारों के उभार ने इस नाम को वज़न दिया, पर उसके मायने पत्थर में नहीं जमे।

panels.shot: medium shot of later genealogists compiling scrolls of lineages in a temple archive
panels.action: Centuries later, genealogists sit in a temple archive, stacking scrolls and palm-leaf records, tracing lines from frontier chiefs to proud Rajput houses.

dialogue.text: Later, as Rajput identity took shape, such early medieval genealogies were woven into larger tapestries. The Pratiharas became one thread among many in a new language of warrior lineages.

i18n.hi: बाद में, जब राजपूत पहचान आकार लेने लगी, ऐसी मध्‍यकालीन वंशावलियाँ एक बड़े बुनावट में गुँथीं। प्रतिहार उस नए योद्धा–भाषा में कई धागों में से बस एक धागा बने।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of Nagabhata I before the gates of a massive northern city, hinting at Kannauj beyond
panels.action: Nagabhata I stands before towering city gates on a northern plain, his gaze fixed beyond, while his retinue waits behind him, the hint of a great city’s outline in the haze.

dialogue.text: Nagabhata himself did not yet rule Kannauj, the prize of the north. But his campaigns and alliances laid paths that his successors would follow, turning a frontier house into imperial contenders.

i18n.hi: नगभट्ट खुद अभी कन्नौज – उत्तर का सबसे बड़ा इनाम – पर नहीं बैठा था। पर उसकी मुहिमों और संधियों ने वो रास्ते बना दिए जिन्हें उत्तराधिकारी चलेंगे, और यही सीमा–घराना आगे चलकर साम्राज्य–दावेदार बन जाएगा।

panels.shot: introspective medium close-up of Nagabhata I at dusk on a fort wall, looking toward the north
panels.action: At dusk, Nagabhata I leans on the battlements of his fort, the sky darkening as he looks toward the distant north, the land below him quiet for a moment.

dialogue.speaker: nagabhata_i
dialogue.text: A gate is not a wall; it opens for those who can hold it.

i18n.hi: फाटक दीवार नहीं होता – वो बस उसी के लिए खुलता है जो उसे थाम सके।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from the Gwalior inscription to a modern skyline, blending past and present
panels.action: The view pulls back from the carved Gwalior inscription to reveal, in a soft blend, a modern city skyline rising beyond the old fort walls.

dialogue.text: To trace Nagabhata and the early Pratiharas is to watch origins being crafted in real time—where a title meaning doorkeeper, a shifting name like Gurjara, and a frontier life became the claim to guard an entire north.

i18n.hi: नगभट्ट और शुरुआती प्रतिहारों को पढ़ना मतलब है किसी जन्म को उसी वक्त बनते देखना – जहाँ द्वारपाल जैसा पद, गुर्जर जैसा बदलता नाम, और सरहदी ज़िंदगी मिलकर पूरे उत्तर की रखवाली का दावा बन जाते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Doorkeepers to Guardians of the North
